array.caption.append: Laid it on the end — nothing had to shift
array.caption.base: An array packs equal-width cells side by side with no gaps and calls each one by a number counted from 0 — know the number and you arrive in one step, but touch the middle and the neighbours shift along.
array.caption.handover: Your turn — type an index and a value, then press Read, Write, Insert, Remove, Append or Search.
array.caption.insert: Slid one in at {index} — the {shifted} cells behind it each moved one place along
array.caption.limitReached: Reached the teaching limit of {maxSize} — no further {op} is possible
array.caption.outOfRange: That position is out of range ({op} {index}) — nothing happens on the strip
array.caption.read: Jumped straight to cell {index} — one "start + {index}" reaches {value}
array.caption.remove: Emptied {index} — the {shifted} cells behind it each pulled one place back
array.caption.resize: The cells are full — moving {copied} of them onto a new strip twice the size
array.caption.searchMiss: Not found — scanned the whole strip
array.caption.write: Replaced the value in cell {index} — the neighbours are untouched
hashTableChaining.caption.alphaWarn: The table is getting cramped — it will need to grow soon.
hashTableChaining.caption.base: A hash table lays out a row of identical slots and a function box throws each key into the one slot it picks — when two land on the same slot, a chain grows there.
hashTableChaining.caption.collision: Two landed on the same slot — the chain grows by one.
hashTableChaining.caption.duplicate: key {key} is already on that chain.
hashTableChaining.caption.emptyTableOp: The table is empty — there is no key to search for or remove.
hashTableChaining.caption.handover: Your turn — type a key, then press Insert, Search or Remove.
hashTableChaining.caption.insert: Threw the key into the slot the function chose.
hashTableChaining.caption.rehashBegin: The table got cramped — growing it and throwing everything again.
hashTableChaining.caption.rehashEnd: Grew the table and threw everything again — α is back in the safe range.
hashTableChaining.caption.removeStart: The function box points at a slot — taking it off there.
hashTableChaining.caption.searchFound: One jump plus {walked} comparisons — arrived at {key} in index {index}.
hashTableChaining.caption.searchMiss: That key is not on this slot's chain.
hashTableChaining.caption.searchStart: The function box points at a slot — now walking that slot's chain.
hashTableChaining.label.auxProbingNote: it squeezes sideways and moves on
hashTableChaining.label.auxRehashNote: the main view shows the new table, the side panel the old one
linkedListSingly.caption.base: In a linked list every node holds a single finger pointing only at its own next — inserting or removing is not moving cards around but cutting and retying two or three fingers.
linkedListSingly.caption.handover: Your turn — type an index and a value, then press Insert, Remove or Search.
linkedListSingly.caption.headSlideNew: The head label glided over to the new card.
linkedListSingly.caption.headSlideSecond: The head label glided over to the second card.
linkedListSingly.caption.insertBindNext: Tied the new card's finger to the next card first.
linkedListSingly.caption.insertHeadBind: Tied the new card's finger to the old first card.
linkedListSingly.caption.insertLimit: Reached the teaching limit — no more cards can be threaded in.
linkedListSingly.caption.insertRewirePre: Moved the previous card's finger over to the new card.
linkedListSingly.caption.removeRewire: Moved the previous card's finger straight on to the next card.
linkedListSingly.caption.searchFound: Found it after {walked} steps — {value} at index {index}
linkedListSingly.caption.searchMiss: Walked to the end, and that value was not there.
linkedListSingly.caption.searchStart: Starting at the head — following the fingers one step at a time.
lruCache.caption.base: An LRU cache shares one set of nodes between a hash map (key → node) and a doubly linked list (recency order) — every call drags a node to the MRU end, and on overflow the LRU end vanishes from both areas at once.
lruCache.caption.evict: Over capacity — {key} at the LRU end disappears from both areas together.
lruCache.caption.getHit: {key} was dragged to the MRU end — even a get rotates the list.
lruCache.caption.getMiss: {key} is not in the cache — the list stays as it was.
lruCache.caption.handover: Your turn — type a key and value, then press get or put.
lruCache.caption.invalidKey: {op}: only short alphanumeric keys (values) are accepted — got "{raw}"
lruCache.caption.putInsert: New key {key} entered at the MRU end (room to spare).
lruCache.caption.putUpdate: The value for {key} was updated and dragged to the MRU end.
lruCache.label.references: See also: NeetCode 146 · dev.to LRU illustrated · GeeksforGeeks LRU
lruCache.narrative.line1: An LRU cache carves a "recency order" onto a plain key-value store.
lruCache.narrative.line2: The hash slots on top give fast key → node pointer lookup,
lruCache.narrative.line3: while the doubly linked list below carries the order of use.
lruCache.narrative.line4: Both areas share the same nodes, so every call updates the two at once.
lruCache.narrative.line5: Even a get is a write in effect — it drags its node to the MRU end.
lruCache.narrative.line6: A put on a full cache makes the node at the LRU end vanish from both areas together.
stack.caption.base: A stack hands back the most recently added element first — every change happens at one single place, the top.
stack.caption.feedInput: Boxes are waiting on the input track — they will be stacked on top one by one.
stack.caption.handover: Your turn — type a value and press Push, Pop or Peek.
stack.caption.peek: Looked at the top value — the pile is unchanged.
stack.caption.push: Placed a new box on top — {value}
stack.caption.underflow: No box left to take off.
